diseases.name: Bacterial Wilt
diseases.description: A bacterial disease that blocks the water vessels of squash and cucumber, so the plant wilts and dies.
diseases.causes: Striped and spotted cucumber beetles carry the bacteria in their gut and infect plants as they feed.
symptoms: Single leaves wilt and look dull green
Whole runners, then the plant, wilt and do not recover overnight
Cut stems ooze sticky threads when pulled apart
diseases.effect: Wilted plants die within one to two weeks.
diseases.untreated: Beetles keep spreading the bacteria to the rest of the planting.

steps.title: Remove wilted plants
steps.instruction: Pull out and remove wilted plants at once.
steps.rationale: They are a source for the beetles.

steps.title: Control cucumber beetles
steps.instruction: Check plants daily, hand-pick or use netting, and use controls registered locally.

steps.title: Cover young plants
steps.instruction: Use insect netting until flowering (open it for pollinators).
steps.rationale: Young plants are most at risk.

lifecycle: The bacteria overwinter inside cucumber beetles.
Leaves, then the whole plant, wilt and die.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: zucchini bacterial wilt

diseases.name: Downy Mildew
diseases.description: A water-mould disease of cucurbit leaves that spreads fast in humid weather.
diseases.causes: Spores blow in on the wind from infected crops further south; leaf wetness and humid nights let them infect.
symptoms: Angular yellow spots bounded by the leaf veins
Grey to purple downy growth under the spots
Spots turn brown and leaves die from the edges
diseases.effect: Leaves die quickly, so fruit is exposed and poorly filled.
diseases.untreated: An unchecked epidemic can kill the leaves of a whole field within weeks.

steps.title: Remove badly affected leaves
steps.instruction: Take off leaves covered with spots.

steps.title: Keep leaves dry
steps.instruction: Water at the base in the morning, space plants.

steps.title: Protective fungicide
steps.instruction: Spray a registered product for downy mildew following the label.

prevention.title: Follow disease forecasts
prevention.detail: Spores travel long distances on the wind.

lifecycle: Spores blow in from infected crops.
Humid nights let them infect wet leaves.
Angular yellow spots form, grey down underneath.
New spores spread on the wind.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: zucchini downy mildew

diseases.name: Zucchini Yellow Mosaic
diseases.pathogen: Zucchini yellow mosaic virus (ZYMV, a potyvirus)
diseases.description: A virus disease of squash and other cucurbits that mottles and deforms the leaves and fruit.
diseases.causes: Aphids pick up the virus while probing infected plants and pass it on within minutes.
symptoms: Bright yellow and green mosaic on young leaves
diseases.effect: Infected plants grow little and their fruit cannot be sold.
diseases.untreated: Early infection can wipe out a planting.

steps.title: Remove infected plants early
steps.instruction: Pull out mottled, stunted plants and remove them.
steps.rationale: Each one is a source for aphids.

steps.title: Keep aphids away
steps.instruction: Use reflective mulch or netting on young plants.
steps.rationale: Aphids spread the virus too fast for sprays to stop.

steps.title: Control weeds
steps.rationale: Weeds can host the virus and aphids.

lifecycle: Aphids carry the virus from infected plants.
A short probe on a leaf passes it on.
sources: PlantSeg (Wei et al. 2024, CC BY 4.0) class: zucchini yellow mosaic virus
